content: 1. In epidemiological settings such as those in Africa, South Asia, and South-East Asia, what is the feasibility and accuracy of using weight-for-height, mid-upper arm circumference, and reduced growth velocity (weight-for-age), with or without the presence of oedema, to identify infants under 6 months of age who require therapeutic management? 2. What criteria are most effective in identifying infants under 6 months of age who exhibit the metabolic abnormalities or adaptations associated with severe acute malnutrition, as observed in older children? 3. What is the effectiveness, tolerance, and safety of using ready-to-use therapeutic food as an adjunct to breastfeeding in infants under 6 months of age with severe acute malnutrition, including those with oedema, those aged 4–6 months, and those with underlying conditions such as HIV? 4. What is the recommended folic acid supplementation for infants under 6 months of age who are diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition? 5. Are there any necessary adjustments in drug dosages or the selection of drugs when managing infants under 6 months of age with severe acute malnutrition? 6. Is there any evidence to suggest that the efficacy of vitamin A supplementation in infants under 6 months of age with severe acute malnutrition differs from that observed in infants aged 1 to 5 months who do not have severe acute malnutrition?
